findings.title: Nudge token that becomes the payment token: the entire accumulated nudge pot is swept to an arbitrary batchMint caller via the ungated dust refund

location.firstPartyContribution: src/dispatchers/NudgeRatchet.sol, src/dispatchers/Uniboost.sol, src/dispatchers/PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol — three USDC-prime donors feeding a USDC nudge stream

findings.rootCauseClass: config-coupled value misdirection across contracts (payment-token / nudge-token collision + ungated dust sweep)

poc.headline: 1-wei payment, count=1, unprivileged caller extracts 190.0 USDC of a 200 USDC pot; repeatable (second call took a further 100 USDC); control arm before the repoint extracts 0
amplifiersObservedBeyondTier2: The mint itself is funded out of the pot (step-6 unbounded allowance to nftMinter), so extraction is exactly pot - mintPrice and the caller needs no payment budget.
_payRewards never runs (count 1 < nudgeSize 5 => qualifies == false); value leaves via the step-10 dust sweep, which is NOT gated on qualifies.

findings.impact: The whole standing nudge pot, funded by prior minters, is transferable to whoever calls batchMint next, for 1 wei and count=1, bypassing the nudgeSize earn-your-nudge gate entirely. Permissionless first-come race, repeatable every time the pot refills, and continuous while misconfigured because collectNudge settles into the batch-minter on every donation. Trigger is a single ordinary owner tx (setDispatcherIndex / setTokenMinter) on a topology where three of four in-scope dispatchers prime in USDC.
findings.notCreatedByThisRange: The pre-change safeTransfer landed USDC on the batch-minter the same way. Stories 046/047 enlarge the quiet-accumulation window and remove the owner's interception path (NudgeStreamer has no rescue of its own).
findings.scopeCaveat: SANITIZER/HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED. The literal root-cause lines are in the project's own nested lib/ (phoenix-nft-staking), which C4 'root cause OOS' would normally exclude. Counter-argument preserved per Law 1: the collision is created entirely by first-party dispatcher topology (three USDC-prime donors) and by the first-party decision to keep feeding it; it is filed as an integration hazard against the first-party callers, not against the dep. Do not silently drop on the OOS rule — if it is excluded, exclude it visibly with this reasoning attached, and consider re-filing it on the phoenix-nft-staking ledger.
findings.suggestedRemedy: Treat 'primeToken() of the newly pinned dispatcher is not in getNudgeTokens()' as a hard precondition of every setDispatcherIndex/setTokenMinter; unwhitelist first (after draining per DEDUP-19-05). Upstream: gate the step-10 dust sweep on qualifies, or exclude nudge-whitelisted balances from it.

findings.title: NudgeRatchetDelayRelease.release() still lump-transfers to the batch-minter and is 100% back-runnable — the anti-burst invariant stories 046/047 advertise is not enforced on the fifth donor
findings.rootCauseClass: incomplete invariant coverage / MEV on a cross-contract value handoff

poc.headline: 50,000 USDC lump captured 100% in the same block (no vm.warp) by a searcher calling batchMint(count=5, minRewards=[50000e6]); honest next batcher receives 0
poc.contrastArm: test_T4_contrast_streamedDonorIsNotBurstCapturable — the same 50,000 USDC routed via NudgeRatchet through the streamer yields the same-block back-runner exactly 0, with >= LUMP-1 still buffered. Direct empirical demonstration that the invariant holds on the four streamed donors and not on the fifth.

crossReference.F-03-046: Law-2 spec-conformance framing of the SAME root cause (the fifth donor is un-routed). KEEP F-03-046 in the spec-conformance report; do NOT count it as a second security finding. Total security findings arising from this root cause: one.

findings.impact: The entire released lump is capturable by a single same-block back-runner. release() is onlyReleaser and therefore an identifiable, mempool-visible transaction. Loss falls on the honest batchers who would otherwise have shared the value over the stream window. Design-coverage gap, not a regression: DelayRelease behaves as it always did — the finding is that four contracts' NatSpec now advertise the property as system-wide while the path most exposed to it is uncovered, so a reviewer reading only the four changed files concludes the property holds.
findings.mitigatingContext: release is onlyReleaser, so burst timing is admin-chosen rather than attacker-chosen, and the contract is itself a manual rate-control throttle. Same MEV class as phoenix-nft-staking ledger 858e9e80 (wont-fix) — DO NOT collapse into it: different contract, different repo, different fingerprint.
findings.suggestedRemedy: Route release() through collectNudge (one-line, same shape as NudgeRatchet), or add explicit NatSpec stating this dispatcher is deliberately outside the streamer because it already provides admin rate control.

findings.title: NudgeRatchet's mandatory streamer wedges every mint at that index AND makes resident USDC unreachable — the L-08 fix is intact but its recoverability rationale expired
findings.location: src/dispatchers/NudgeRatchet.sol:_dispatch:156-161 (rationale at :112-133); no rescueERC20 anywhere on the contract
findings.rootCauseClass: liveness coupling across a trust boundary + escape-hatch rationale invalidated by a later change

exactReverts: nudgeStreamer == address(0) (the post-deploy default) => Error("NudgeRatchet: nudgeStreamer unset")
poc.unreachabilityProof: test_T2c_residentUsdcIsUnreachable_noRescueSelector — with 500 USDC resident, an owner raw call to rescueERC20(address,address,uint256) returns false (selector absent); positive control: the identical call on a freshly deployed NudgeRatchetDelayRelease returns true. The only forwarding path (dispatch) is itself reverting. 500 USDC still on the ratchet at end of test.
poc.thirdPartyTriggerBeyondTier2: test_T2d_blacklistOnStreamerBricksEveryDonor — blacklisting the STREAMER address on a USDC stand-in bricks NudgeRatchet and Uniboost alike (one blacklisting, every donor sharing the streamer) AND permanently strands the already-buffered pooled funds, because pullPendingStream reverts on _settle's outbound transfer and NudgeStreamer has no owner rescue.

ledgerReconciliation.classification: EXPIRED CLOSURE — not a regression, and NOT an incomplete fix
ledgerReconciliation.detail: L-08 ('NudgeRatchet has no rescueERC20; out-of-band USDC is permanently stranded') was closed by story-038 on the owner's stated alternative: a full-balance sweep in _dispatch (require(bal >= amount); forward the whole balanceOf). That code is INTACT at d4cc563 (verified src/dispatchers/NudgeRatchet.sol:142-162). The closure was explicitly judged 'on whether out-of-band USDC becomes recoverable, NOT on literal rescueERC20 presence' (quoted from the L-08 triage note). Story-046 made the sweep's only delivery leg an external cross-repo call that can revert — so the recoverability property the closure rested on no longer holds whenever the streamer path is broken. The RATIONALE expired; the patch did not regress. Reviewers must NOT be sent to restore the sweep — it is there. Reconcile against L-08 (reopen candidate), do not mint a fresh fingerprint for the strand half.

findings.impact: Two compounding effects while the streamer path is broken: (1) every user mint through that dispatcher index reverts (NudgeRatchet is the only one of five donors with no try/catch, no donationSplit, and a batchMinter that cannot be zeroed — any non-zero balance forces the streamer branch unconditionally), and (2) any USDC resident on the ratchet is unreachable by any actor, because there is no rescue and the only forwarding path is the reverting dispatch. Availability plus a conditional permanent strand. Trigger set is a strict superset of the pre-change safeTransfer failure surface and now includes a third-party failure that did not previously exist (a USDC blacklist on the streamer, which is shared across donors).
findings.authorPreDeclaration: The contract NatSpec pre-declares the wedge 'NOT an audit finding'. Per Law 1 the author's say-so does not auto-suppress; the reasoning tier adjudicates. That declaration covers the deliberate liveness coupling. It does NOT cover the second-order consequence — the escape hatch was omitted on a rationale that no longer holds — which is reportable on its merits and is the load-bearing half of this entry.
findings.suggestedRemedy: Restore a real escape hatch (rescueERC20, or an owner-callable sweep that does not depend on collectNudge succeeding); and/or mirror the other three donors with a donation-disable so a mis-wire degrades rather than bricks.

findings.title: PromotionUniV2_Eth._legB swaps the contract's whole ETH balance, so minPromoOut no longer bounds the swap — fork-proved to flip a sandwich from reverting to profitable
findings.rootCauseClass: unbounded input to a slippage-floored swap

poc.result: CONFIRMED still live after the 6-arg pool() rework, 3/3 pass
poc.harness: Mainnet fork @ block 25,550,000 — live UniV2 router/factory, Sky PSM, sUSDS ERC-4626, Balancer V3. No mocked AMM.

measurements.postPoolDispatcherBalance: 0 (entire balance swapped, not the leg output)

poc.decisiveDifferential: T5b vs T5c use an IDENTICAL minPromoOut = 478.315e18 (what an honest off-chain pooler computes for the leg's own ETH, 1% tolerance) and an IDENTICAL 12 ETH sandwich. Without stray ETH, pool() REVERTS UniswapV2Router: INSUFFICIENT_OUTPUT_AMOUNT — the floor does its job. With 1.61794 ETH stray resident, pool() SUCCEEDS and the sandwicher exits with +0.29677 ETH profit.

ledgerReconciliation.twin: F-01-044 (also wont-fix, same date, same site)
ledgerReconciliation.classification: DO NOT FILE A NEW FINDING. Reconcile against L-13 and attach the new evidence.
ledgerReconciliation.quotedTriageReason: "finding is valid but the whole-balance ETH sweep in PromotionUniV2_Eth._legB (swaps address(this).balance) plus the open receive() is a DESIRED FEATURE the owner intends to keep, not a defect to fix. Non-theft (Tier-3 INV-4 fork-proved donated ETH only ever reaches protocol-owned LP, never a third party). ..."
ledgerReconciliation.reFileBasis: MATERIAL: the run-19 T5 fork evidence directly contradicts the load-bearing clause of that closure. The wont-fix rests on 'non-theft — donated ETH only ever reaches protocol-owned LP, never a third party'. T5c shows a third party (a sandwicher) extracting +0.29677 ETH in a scenario that is IDENTICAL except for the stray balance, and T5b shows the honest floor would have rejected that same sandwich. The loss channel is not the donated ETH's destination (which is indeed protocol-owned LP); it is the 11x dilution of the pooler's slippage floor, which INV-4 did not test. The stale-residual case needs no attacker at all — rescueETH's own NatSpec concedes a partial Leg B leaves resident ETH. Recommend surfacing this to the owner for re-triage of L-13/F-01-044 with the T5b/T5c differential attached. Never silently override the reclassNote; the owner re-decides.

findings.impact: The caller-supplied minPromoOut is calibrated off-chain for the expected 30%-leg ETH. Resident or third-party-donated ETH inflates the swapped amount without inflating the floor, so the floor stops bounding the trade and the swap is exposed to a strictly larger sandwich than the pooler priced. A griefer must fund the excess themselves (cost-bearing, not free), but a stale residual from a prior partial pool() reaches the same state with no attacker at all.

findings.lawNote: Law 3 — non-obvious consequence of a routine, well-intentioned owner action. In scope as an operational hazard, NOT a malicious-owner vector.
findings.title: Retiring a (batchMinter, token) stream permanently strands one duration's worth of donations; four routine tidy-up actions each close the only recovery path, and nothing in the system surfaces the buffer
findings.location: src/dispatchers/{BalancerPoolerV2,NudgeRatchet,Uniboost,PromotionUniV2_Eth}.sol — setBatchMinter / setRecipient / setNudgeStreamer, acting on NudgeStreamer buffer state (lib/phoenix-nft-staking/src/NudgeStreamer.sol)
findings.rootCauseClass: cross-contract stranded value / retirement-ordering footgun with no observability surface
findings.supportingTier3: T3 measured the exposed quantity empirically: the resident buffer converges to exactly one stream window's inflow (99.98% of D*duration/dt at 8 windows), is cadence-independent, and drains to exactly 0 one window after donations stop. So the amount at risk at retirement is precisely B* = rho * D.

mechanism.noRescue: NudgeStreamer has no owner rescue or sweep — verified exhaustively against its complete function list (registerStream, collectNudge, pullPendingStream, pendingStream, _settle, _accrued). Buffered value leaves only via _settle, reachable two ways: a donor calling collectNudge for that same pair, or the batchMinter itself calling pullPendingStream (which BatchNFTMinterMultiToken does in exactly one place, inside batchMint).
mechanism.atRetirement: Once the dispatcher is repointed or disabled, path 1 stops and the residual depends entirely on path 2, which requires ALL of: not paused; tokenMinter != 0; dispatcherIndex != 0 and resolving non-zero; token still on _nudgeTokens; someone paying for >= 1 real mint. pause(), setTokenMinter(0), setDispatcherIndex(0), or unwhitelisting the token each destroys it. _resolvePaymentPath runs at step 2, BEFORE the step-3.5 flush, so unsetting either pointer reverts batchMint before the flush is ever reached.
mechanism.blindnessOfExistingRunbook: The project has already executed a batch-minter migration (MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol) whose documented retirement step is 'neutralize the old instance' and whose pot recovery reads balanceOf(oldBatchMinter) — structurally blind to the streamer buffer. That script predates the streamer, so a future migration written to the same template silently drops B*.

sizing.formula: B* = rho * D — one duration's worth of donation flow, independent of cadence
sizing.observedRate: ~77.6 USDC per 40-batch at the 15% batchDonationSize (derived from mainnet tx 0x6d71d6fd...f14996, block 25242986)
sizing.grid: 11 USDC (D=1d, weekly batches) to 4,656 USDC (D=30d, 2 batches/day). Order 10^2-10^3 USDC at observed rates.
sizing.unknown: The mainnet stream duration is NOT set anywhere in the reviewed repos — it is a live ops parameter passed to registerStream. Every figure scales linearly with it. See MANUAL-REVIEW MR-01.

findings.impact: One duration's worth of the protocol's own nudge incentive budget becomes permanently unreachable by any actor. Affected parties: future batch-minters. Recovery done in the RIGHT order is cheap (wait >= D, one batchMint(1) on the old instance flushes the whole buffer, then rescueERC20 — total cost ~13 USDS plus gas), which is exactly why it is a footgun rather than a loss: the owner must know to do it, must do it before any of the four tidy-up actions, and nothing surfaces the buffer — no event fires at retirement, no dispatcher view exposes it, and the only read is NudgeStreamer.pendingStream(oldBatchMinter, token), which a migration operator has no reason to call.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Before retiring a batch-minter or repointing a dispatcher's batchMinter/recipient: (a) repoint the donor first so donations stop; (b) wait >= duration; (c) call pendingStream(oldBatchMinter, token) and confirm it equals the whole buffer; (d) run one batchMint(1, ...) on the old instance to flush it; (e) rescueERC20 the proceeds; ONLY THEN pause / unset tokenMinter / unset dispatcherIndex / unwhitelist the token. This belongs in the dispatchers' ops NatSpec.
findings.confidence: high on mechanism, high on irrecoverability, medium on whether an operator would actually trip it

findings.lawNote: Law 3. The DEPLOY-ORDERING case is correctly out of scope (fails loudly on the first dispatch, before user traffic — obvious to a competent operator, suppress). The REPOINT case is in scope.
findings.title: Repointing batchMinter/recipient, or enabling a dormant donation, silently arms NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered on every subsequent user mint; clearing it requires calls on two other contracts in another repository
findings.rootCauseClass: cross-repo config precondition with no local guard and no view that surfaces it
findings.supportingTier3: Tier-3 recorded a FOURTH independent reproduction of this class, on PromotionUniV2_Eth: with the Q-17 arity repaired, test_guided_sequence_holdsAllInvariants compiles and then fails at runtime with 'PromotionUniV2_Eth: nudgeStreamer unset' because the pre-story-046 harness never wires a streamer.

distinctFrom.DEDUP-19-02: KEPT SEPARATE deliberately. On Uniboost / PromotionUniV2_Eth the wedge is availability-only, owner-recoverable, tx-atomic, with no value at risk and a config.disabled backstop at NFTMinterV2 — a Law-3 footgun. On NudgeRatchet it additionally strands funds with no rescue path at all (DEDUP-19-02), which is a different impact requiring a different mitigation. Same pattern, different root-cause consequence and different fix — Keep Both under the dedup rules.
distinctFrom.fourthReproduction: The PromotionUniV2_Eth Q-17 runtime failure is an INSTANCE of this finding, not a distinct finding. It is the same root cause (mandatory streamer + unenforced wiring) on a contract that degrades gracefully. Recorded as an instance; the harness-side consequence is filed separately as DEDUP-19-12.

findings.impact: setBatchMinter(new) / setRecipient(new) on a live dispatcher succeeds silently and arms NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered() on every subsequent user mint — the product cannot be sold until config is corrected. No value is lost (the user's payment happens inside the same reverting tx). Clearing it requires batchMinter.setNudgeTokenWhitelist(token, true) then NudgeStreamer.registerStream(...), the latter onlyOwner of a contract in a DIFFERENT repository that may not share the dispatcher's owner key. The dispatcher exposes no view and no guard that would surface the missing registration before it bites, and setBatchMinter does not check it. A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised => footgun, in scope.
findings.authorPreDeclaration: The shipped NatSpec says this is 'the accepted consequence of the mandatory-streamer decision, NOT an audit finding'. Assessed on its merits: correct for the deploy-ordering case, over-broad for the repoint case. A story cannot pre-declare a hazard out of scope. Correct disposition is 'known, accepted, recorded as an operational hazard with safe-config guidance', not 'not a finding'. No Law-1 escalation: no exploit, no value loss, no unrecoverable state.
findings.suggestedRemedy: Have setBatchMinter/setRecipient optionally probe INudgeStreamer(nudgeStreamer).pendingStream(newSink, token) — a registered pair is a cheap positive signal — or ship a runbook item binding the sink repoint to the registerStream call.

findings.lawNote: Law 3 — two non-obvious consequences of ordinary config actions on BalancerPoolerV2.
findings.title: BalancerPoolerV2: disabling the donation removes parked USDS from the automatic retry loop, and psm.gem() is read live so a setPSM repoint silently changes the token identity handed to collectNudge
findings.rootCauseClass: config-coupling / recoverability + live-read of mutable external config

subInstances.detail: The sweep-and-retry that recovers parked USDS lives INSIDE `if (donationEnabled)`. If the owner disables the donation (setBatchDonationSize(0) or setBatchMinter(0)) while USDS is parked from earlier skips, that USDS is never re-swept, never wrapped into sUSDS, stops being productive collateral, and does not contribute to pool(). Recoverable only via rescueERC20:437 — which the owner must know to call, while the NatSpec (:257-261) presents re-sweeping as THE recovery mechanism without noting it is conditional on the donation staying enabled.

`address gem = ISkyPSM(psm).gem()` is read live on every call and psm is owner-settable. A setPSM repoint to a PSM with a different gem yields an unregistered (batchMinter, newGem) pair => NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered => caught => USDS parks quietly behind one DonationSkipped event. Fully recoverable (repoint back, or register the new pair) but silent until someone reads the event stream — and per DEDUP-19-08 that event stream is the only signal. Note the asymmetry: PromotionUniV2_Eth pins USDC as a constant and NudgeRatchet pins an immutable 6-dp token; BalancerPoolerV2 is the SOLE live-read of the four.

findings.impact: Parked USDS silently leaves the productive-collateral set and the automatic recovery loop; no value is destroyed (rescueERC20 reaches it) but the NatSpec's stated recovery mechanism is conditional in a way the NatSpec does not say. Backing is not impaired in either sub-instance.
findings.suggestedRemedy: Move the sweep-and-retry outside the donationEnabled gate; pair every setPSM with a registerStream for the new gem, or pin the gem at construction as the sibling dispatchers do.

findings.title: The repo's entire test tree did not compile at d4cc563 — every existing regression test was unrunnable (Q-17 escalation)
findings.location: test/Tier3PromotionInvariants.t.sol:120 — disp.pool(amountIn, 0, 0, 0, 0) against the current 6-arg signature
findings.rootCauseClass: test bit-rot with repo-wide blast radius
findings.evidence: forge build failed at d4cc563 until run-19 repaired the arity in place (inline `// run-19: Q-17 bit-rot repair` comment, workspace clone only, lib/ untouched). Q-17 remains only PARTIALLY addressed: with the arity fixed, test_guided_sequence_holdsAllInvariants now compiles and fails at runtime with 'PromotionUniV2_Eth: nudgeStreamer unset' — the harness predates story-046 and never wires a NudgeStreamer (it uses a plain EOA as batchMinter). Left unrepaired deliberately; T5 covers the same property against live state.

ledgerReconciliation.classification: STILL OPEN, and the blast radius is larger than the entry states. Q-17 was filed as 'the reworked split/burn/WBTC flow is not fuzzed'. The correct statement at d4cc563 is that the compile failure made the WHOLE suite — every regression test in the repo — unrunnable. Update the entry's note rather than filing a new one.
ledgerReconciliation.carriedRepair: The arity fix exists only in workspace/yield-claim-nft. It is not in lib/ and is not upstream.

findings.impact: No security impact directly, but for the duration of the bit-rot the project had zero executable regression coverage — every prior finding's guard test was silently not running. Ranked above the remaining QA items for that reason.

findings.title: BalancerPoolerV2's dust branch went event-silent at the exact moment DonationSkipped became the sole signal for a much wider failure set, while the NatSpec still names dust as a DonationSkipped trigger
findings.detail: The require used to revert into the caller's catch, which emitted DonationSkipped(remainingUSDS). The if returns normally and emits NOTHING — neither BatchDonatedViaPSM nor DonationSkipped. Simultaneously the caught region's CONTENTS widened from PSM-only to PSM + streamer wiring + the streamer's own outbound settle transfer (newly swallowed: "nudgeStreamer unset", NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered(), NudgeStreamer__NotWhitelisted(), failures inside _settle's outbound transfer, a non-conforming/EOA streamer), so every distinct wiring failure collapses into one undifferentiated DonationSkipped. The guard itself is load-bearing and CORRECT — it keeps NudgeStreamer__ZeroAmount() out of the catch. The defect is purely that the contract's documented observability contract was not updated in the same commit, and the same commit doubles down by telling operators to 'watch DonationSkipped and the contract's USDS balance'.

crossReference.F-01-047: Law-2 spec-conformance framing of the SAME root cause (documented behaviour deviation). KEEP F-01-047 in the spec-conformance report; do NOT count it as a second finding here.
crossReference.storyAuthorisation: The code change is authorised by story-047 bullet 4 ('a clean no-op instead of a caught revert'), so this is not an unauthorised behaviour change.

findings.impact: Observability, not value. _psmDonate is atomic so nothing is stranded mid-route, the parked USDS is re-swept by the next successful dispatch, and phUSD backing is NOT impaired (the un-donated USDS stays on the pooler and is still protocol-held collateral). What silently dies is the batch-minter reward: a streamer misconfiguration can run indefinitely while the nudge incentive is dead and hook.onDispatch keeps accruing mint-debt on the gross amount. The dust condition itself requires a sub-1e-6-USDC sweep.
findings.sameShapeElsewhere: The event-silent skip shape exists NATIVELY (not as a delta) at Uniboost.sol:246 and PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol:392.
findings.suggestedRemedy: Emit DonationSkipped(usdsAmount) from the else of the guard, or strike 'dust' from the event NatSpec and say so in the ops note. Separately, differentiate the swallowed failure causes in the catch.

findings.title: Uniboost's prime token is unconstrained and now transits a third-party contract's transferFrom + transfer pair with no failure isolation
findings.rootCauseClass: widened trust surface on an unvalidated token / missing deploy-time guard
findings.detail: NudgeRatchet and NudgeRatchetDelayRelease both enforce decimals() == 6 at construction. Uniboost takes primeToken_ as a free constructor argument with no guard at all. Post-story-046 the donation branch has no try/catch, so a live donation's success depends on TWO token movements inside a foreign contract (safeTransferFrom Uniboost->streamer at NudgeStreamer.sol:149, and safeTransfer streamer->recipient at :187) instead of one leaf transfer. Consequences for a non-plain prime token: a blacklisting token that blocks either the streamer or the recipient bricks every mint through this dispatcher.

routedSubClaims.claim: Reentrancy premise. collectNudge fires an OUTBOUND transfer to the batchMinter inside _settle (:187) BEFORE pulling the donor's tokens (:149) — a hook-bearing token would get control mid-collect, inside the dispatcher's own dispatch. Defences verified adequate (dispatch is contract-wide nonReentrant so pool() shares the lock; collectNudge and pullPendingStream are nonReentrant; _settle is CEI-correct; ERC-1820 is unregistered on all three parties so ERC777 hooks would not fire). Token identity is pinned for three of four donors. Uniboost is the exception, so the 'hook-free token' premise is a DEPLOYMENT POLICY there, not a contract guarantee. No exploit today; recorded as an assumption the deployment must keep true.

FoT cross-stream twist — routed rather than auto-suppressed, and NOT the ordinary FoT class. Generic FoT is permanently C4-invalid on this project family and stays invalid. The distinct claim: collectNudge credits s.buffer += amount with no balance-delta measurement, and the streamer holds ALL streams in one token balance. Its solvency invariant (sum(buffers) == held balance) is justified precisely by 'every buffer is only credited by an actual transferFrom of that same amount'. One FoT/rebasing token admitted through Uniboost's unrestricted prime breaks that invariant, so _settle for one stream could draw down ANOTHER stream's backing. Cross-stream contamination != ordinary FoT under-crediting. Code-scan's counter-reading: _accrued caps at buffer, so the shortfall lands on the LAST claimant of that pair rather than on other pairs' solvency. The two readings disagree; see MANUAL-REVIEW MR-02.

findings.impact: No exploit at the live topology (USDC). The in-scope point is the missing deploy-time guard plus the removal of failure isolation, on the one donor whose token identity is not pinned — it converts a contract-level guarantee into a deployment-policy assumption for the reentrancy, blacklist, and cross-stream-solvency premises simultaneously.
findings.suggestedRemedy: Mirror NudgeRatchet's constructor guard (decimals()/allowlist), or scope-document the acceptable prime-token set.

findings.title: PromotionUniV2_Eth burns against the leg output but pools against the whole balance, so residual or donated phUSD drifts the documented 30/30 value match
findings.detail: phusdBurned = phusdAcquired / 2 uses Leg A's RETURN VALUE, but _addPhusdPromoLiquidity reads IERC20(phUSD).balanceOf(address(this)) and IERC20(promotionToken).balanceOf(address(this)). Any phUSD resident from a prior pool()'s router refund — or donated by a third party — is pooled without a matching burn. Same for donated promotion token on the other side.
findings.impact: The 'half burned, halves value-matched' property documented at :448-450 holds only for a contract that starts each pool() at a zero phUSD balance. minLP bounds the outcome, so this is an accounting / documentation-fidelity issue rather than a value leak.
findings.relatedButDistinct: Same whole-balance-vs-leg-output SHAPE as DEDUP-19-04, but a different asset (phUSD/promotion token, not ETH), a different consequence (documentation fidelity, not slippage-floor dilution) and a different fix. Keep separate; do not fold into L-13.

findings.title: The streamer forceApprove is the sole unpaired approval in these contracts — safe today only because of an external repo's implementation detail
findings.location: src/dispatchers/BalancerPoolerV2.sol:346 (asymmetric with the PSM allowance zeroed eleven lines earlier at :336), plus NudgeRatchet:160, Uniboost:250, PromotionUniV2_Eth:396
findings.rootCauseClass: hardening / defence-in-depth (NOT a live vector — see REFUTED R-03)
findings.detail: All four donors forceApprove(streamer, exactAmount) and never reset to zero. Every OTHER forceApprove in these contracts (Uniboost:275/279, 300/306; PromotionUniV2_Eth:466/472, 483/485, 503/507; BalancerPoolerV2:336) is paired with a zeroing reset — the streamer approve is the sole unpaired one. The residual is provably zero with the canonical streamer (collectNudge:149 pulls exactly amount in the same call, and any failure rolls back atomically). Exploitability REFUTED (R-03). Retained ONLY as a hardening item because the safe-today property rests entirely on an external, cross-repo contract's implementation detail rather than on any local invariant.
findings.impact: None today. A setNudgeStreamer to an under-pulling implementation would leave a live residual allowance on a USDC-class token. Cheap fix: pair each approve with a zeroing reset, as every other forceApprove in these contracts already does.
findings.note: Filed as QA/hardening precisely so the asymmetry is recorded and not re-derived next run. Not a security finding.

refuted.claim: BalancerPoolerV2._psmDonate:335 discards buyGem's return value; the downstream forceApprove/collectNudge are sized on the locally computed gemAmt rather than USDC actually received.
refuted.reason: ISkyPSM.buyGem(usr, gemAmt) is EXACT-OUTPUT by construction — DssLitePsm transfers exactly gemAmt of gem to usr and returns the DAI/USDS amount PULLED, not the gem amount. Sizing on the locally computed gemAmt is therefore correct, not an assumption. Should a non-conforming PSM ever deliver less, the failure is not a silent shortfall: the streamer's safeTransferFrom(donor, ..., gemAmt) reverts on insufficient balance, the whole _psmDonate rolls back atomically, and _dispatch's catch parks the USDS and emits DonationSkipped. FAILS CLOSED.
refuted.residue: The adjacent live psm.gem() read is a real (separate) hazard and is preserved as DEDUP-19-07(b).

refuted.claim: PromotionUniV2_Eth._addPhusdPromoLiquidity:468 calls addLiquidity(..., 0, 0, address(this), block.timestamp) — zero for both amountAMin and amountBMin.
refuted.reason: minLP is the STRONGER guard, not a weaker substitute. For a UniV2 pair, liquidity = min(amountA*ts/reserveA, amountB*ts/reserveB), so a sandwich that skews the reserve ratio mechanically reduces the LP minted for a fixed pair of input balances; a minLP floor from a fresh quote bounds ratio-skew loss directly in the unit that matters (pool shares), whereas amountMin would only bound the router's refund leg. Three further mitigations verified: pool() is onlyAuthorizedPooler so minLP comes from a permissioned caller; the individual legs already carry minPhusdOut/minEthOut/minPromoOut/minWbtcOut; the sides are value-matched post-burn so the router refund is small and any residual stays for the next pool().
refuted.ledgerEffect: The prior conclusion — amountIn is MEV-neutral, so L-06 stays Low — is UNCHANGED by the 6th minLP parameter; if anything it is now better supported. L-06 and L-15 need no re-weighing on this axis.

refuted.claim: Residual streamer allowance: all four donors forceApprove(streamer, exactAmount) and never reset to zero.
refuted.reason: collectNudge pulls exactly that amount via safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount) (NudgeStreamer.sol:149) in the SAME call, so the standing allowance is zero on success. On any failure the approve is rolled back — atomically inside _psmDonate's try/catch for BalancerPoolerV2, and by the reverting mint for the other three. A non-zero residual requires an under-pulling collectNudge implementation, which only an owner repointing nudgeStreamer at a hostile contract could produce — an obvious owner action (Law 3, suppress).
refuted.residue: The style asymmetry is preserved as a hardening item, DEDUP-19-11. Refuted as a vector, not dropped.

refuted.claim: Two-pointer divergence: if BatchNFTMinterMultiToken's own nudgeStreamer pointer is unset or divergent, every donation accumulates but is NEVER FLUSHED into the nudge pot.
refuted.reason: Not correct. collectNudge calls _settle on EVERY donor deposit (NudgeStreamer.sol:146), and _settle transfers the accrued amount to the batchMinter regardless of whether the batchMinter knows about the streamer. The step-3.5 flush is a freshness optimisation, not the delivery mechanism. With a divergent pointer, throughput and steady state are UNCHANGED; the batcher's snapshot is merely one donation staler and that value goes to a later batcher rather than being lost. A one-batch delay, not a strand. Corollary: there is also NO windfall-on-repair and NO back-run MEV on fixing the pointer.
refuted.disposition: Downgraded to informational. Its only residue is the retirement case, already covered by DEDUP-19-05.

refuted.claim: REWARD-RUNWAY-DEPLETION caller-side rate-drift: collectNudge re-stretches the whole residual buffer over a fresh full duration on every donation, so with one mint per hour and a 7-day duration ~168 donations' worth of USDC is PERMANENTLY resident in the streamer.
refuted.reason: Refuted as a value sink on three counts. (a) Cadence is per BATCH, not per mint — batchMint runs count mints in one transaction so a 40-batch is ONE arrival with dt=0 between its legs; the multiplier is D/dt_batch, not D/dt_mint. (b) Throughput at steady state is 100%: B_{n+1} = B_n*(1 - dt/D) + d has fixed point B* = d*D/dt = rho*D, a working balance, not a growing sink. By Little's Law the mean delivery latency is exactly D — every donated dollar reaches the batch-minter, on average one duration late, which is precisely the mechanism the streamer was built to provide. (c) 'Permanently' is wrong: the rate is frozen at the last deposit (pullPendingStream never recomputes — the load-bearing phlimbo-V1 fix), so accrued = B*elapsed/D reaches B at elapsed = D and the min(accrued, buffer) cap stops it there. No asymptotic tail.
refuted.tier3Measurement: T3, 6/6 pass, real NFTMinterV2.mint calls through the real ratchet into the real streamer. Resident buffer converges to exactly one stream window's inflow (99.98% of D*duration/dt at 8 windows), matching B*(1 - e^{-T/tau}) to the last digit at every cadence over a 200x range; residency as a fraction of cumulative donations is cadence-independent (43.2% +/- 1% at 2 windows) and decays as duration/T; delivered + resident == donated asserted on every row (nothing lost); test_T3_tailDrainsFullyAfterDonationsStop drains the streamer to EXACTLY 0 one window after donations stop. NO RATE DRIFT — the phlimbo-V1 linear-depletion pathology does not reproduce here.
refuted.disposition: Record as MEASURED-AND-CLEAN, not a finding. Its only live residue is the retirement edge, DEDUP-19-05.
refuted.deltaVsPreChange: Per-batch capture at steady state is IDENTICAL to the pre-change safeTransfer (rho*dt). The change is a one-off deferral of one duration's flow plus a permanent reduction in the STANDING balance by the same amount. The pot is not systematically under-funded; stories 046/047 are economically neutral in the steady state.

refuted.claim: Accrued mint-debt vs delivered-value gap: hook.onDispatch fires on the gross amount regardless of donation outcome, so the quiet-skip surface could mint unbacked phUSD.
refuted.reason: phUSD backing is not impaired in ANY of the three failure modes and the value never leaves the system. Streamed successfully: the donation sits in the streamer buffer, still on-chain, still owned by the (batchMinter, token) stream — relocation, not loss. Caught and skipped: the USDS never leaves BalancerPoolerV2, parks on the dispatcher and is re-swept by the next dispatch (or rescueERC20'd) — relocation, not loss. Dust branch: sub-1-unit gemAmt only; the USDS stays put. Sizing the worst case: the donation is batchDonationSize = 15% of dispatched amount and the other 85% is wrapped to sUSDS and pooled regardless, so even total permanent loss of every donation could not move backing by more than 15% of dispatched value — comfortably inside the >=2:1 over-backing cushion prior runs established for DEDUP-001.
refuted.residue: The observability half is real and is preserved as DEDUP-19-08. No unbacked-phUSD path found.

refuted.reason: There is no hash. The site is string(abi.encodePacked(...)) building a JSON metadata literal for uri(); the three dynamic strings are separated by non-empty JSON delimiters ('","image":"' etc.) and the result is never hashed or used as a key. The hash-collision detector class does not apply. Additionally this exact site is already ledgered as Q-01/Q-03 ('abi.encodePacked used to build dynamic-string metadata in uri() (cosmetic)', qa-bundled) — so it is also an EXACT DUPLICATE of an existing entry. Reconcile to Q-03; do not re-file.

cleanVerdicts.verdict: CLEAN — independently confirmed by three tiers

cleanVerdicts.verdict: CLEAN — adjudicated at pattern tier and re-derived independently at econ tier
cleanVerdicts.basis: Every rounding decision on the changed paths floors AGAINST the recipient and FOR the protocol: gemAmt floors (never over-buys, residual USDS re-swept); usdsSpent floors and is <= usdsAmount (protocol keeps the dust); donationAmount = amount*split/100 floors (donates less); rewardPerSecond floors (under-emits); accrued floors and is capped at buffer (the streamer can never pay more than it holds). No asymmetric pair, no profitable loop, no symmetric/half rounding. These are one-way donor paths with NO redemption leg, so the classic round-trip drain has no surface here. Also closes PATTERN-M04 (DIVISION-PRECISION) as intended and protocol-favouring.

cleanVerdicts.verdict: CLEAN — full checklist walked, every row cleared with a stated basis
cleanVerdicts.basis: Classic single-fn (no donor writes local state after collectNudge; only an emit follows; dispatch is nonReentrant). Cross-contract A->B->A (OZ ReentrancyGuard is contract-wide, so pool() is locked for the duration of dispatch; _psmDonate is external but self-gated and unreachable except from _dispatch). Cross-function siblings (same contract-wide guard). Read-only (no donor exposes a price/share view consumed as an oracle; there is no inbound callback window at all because USDC/USDS have no transfer hooks). ERC721 (N/A). ERC1155 receive (cleared non-trivially: NFTMinterV2._executeMint:196 invokes onERC1155Received on an attacker-controlled recipient while the batch-minter's unbounded paymentToken allowance to nftMinter is live, but _executeMint:183 always pulls via safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, ...) so a re-entering attacker spends their OWN funds; mintFor is authorizedMinters-gated; batchMint is nonReentrant; the hook can reach the permissionless collectNudge but the batcher's payout was snapshotted pre-loop so a mid-loop donation cannot be recovered in that same batch). ERC777 (neither donor nor recipient nor streamer registers an ERC-1820 interface).
cleanVerdicts.statedPrecondition: The read-only clearance rests entirely on the token being hook-free — true by pinning for three of four donors, a deployment policy for Uniboost (DEDUP-19-09).

cleanVerdicts.verdict: HOLDS under the new quiet-skip surface
cleanVerdicts.basis: Worst case is bounded by batchDonationSize = 15% of dispatched value; the other 85% is wrapped to sUSDS and pooled regardless of donation outcome. Even total permanent loss of every donation stays comfortably inside the >=2:1 over-backing cushion prior runs established. No re-escalation warranted; the suppression stands.

The step-3.5 flush happens BEFORE the pre-loop snapshot (BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:445-453) and a batcher's own donations enter the streamer only during the step-7 mint loop — AFTER that flush, at elapsed == 0. So a batch cannot settle its own in-loop donations back to itself. No regression of that class. T3's side observation supports the design goal: claimable-right-now is always ~one donation (~8.65 USDC) regardless of cadence or how large the buffer has grown.

cleanVerdicts.class: PATTERN-005 mitigation framing (recorded so the mitigation is neither miscredited nor understated)
cleanVerdicts.verdict: CORRECTED FRAMING — the streamer is a RATE cap: delay, not denial
cleanVerdicts.basis: PATTERN-005 said 'timing throttle, not a value cap' — half right, and the wrong half matters. It is correctly NOT a cap on what one caller can EVENTUALLY take (the batchMinter flushes then snapshots its whole balance, winner-take-all). But it IS a hard cap on the RATE: a batcher's step-3.5 flush yields min(elapsed/D, 1) * buffer, so capturing the whole buffer requires waiting a full D with no intervening claimant. Consequence for triage: any reasoning that treats this hop as an anti-over-funding VALUE cap (cf. phoenix-nft-staking run-22 aggregate-nudge over-funding) is unsupported by the implementation. Story-faithfulness independently confirms no dispatcher NatSpec, story line, or CLAUDE.md text claims it is a cap — so the code was NOT written under a wrong model of the dependency, and there is no Law-2 defect on this axis. DO NOT read this range as closing any pre-existing phoenix-nft-staking nudge over-funding or aggregate-pot finding.

manualReview.reason: unknown-parameter — sizes an active finding, cannot be resolved from source
manualReview.detail: The mainnet stream `duration` is NOT set anywhere in the reviewed repos — it is a live ops parameter passed to registerStream. Every quantity in DEDUP-19-05's sizing scales LINEARLY with it (11 USDC at D=1d/weekly batches, 4,656 USDC at D=30d/2-per-day). This is the single unknown that sizes DEDUP-19-05 and it should be pinned in the deploy runbook. Choosing D is choosing how much value sits one config-mistake away from being stranded; D should be set no longer than the smoothing actually needed. Batch cadence is likewise not observable from source, hence a scenario grid rather than a point estimate.
manualReview.askOfHuman: Supply the live registerStream duration (and observed batch cadence) so DEDUP-19-05 can be sized rather than bracketed.

manualReview.reason: two tiers disagree on the blast radius — flagged for human adjudication rather than resolved by the deduplicator
manualReview.detail: Cross-stream FoT contamination. Pattern tier: NudgeStreamer holds ALL streams in one token balance and credits s.buffer += amount with no balance-delta measurement, so one FoT/rebasing token admitted through Uniboost's unrestricted prime breaks the sum(buffers) == held balance invariant and _settle for one stream could draw down ANOTHER stream's backing. Code tier: _accrued caps at buffer, so the shortfall lands on the LAST claimant of that pair, not on other pairs' solvency. These are different claims about where the loss lands. Both agree there is no exploit at the live USDC topology.
manualReview.whyNotDropped: Generic FoT is permanently C4-invalid on this project family and stays invalid — but cross-stream contamination is a DIFFERENT claim (a shared-balance solvency invariant, not per-transfer under-crediting), and it would only surface if a non-plain token were ever admitted. Carried as the hardening rationale inside DEDUP-19-09 and parked here so the disagreement is visible.
manualReview.askOfHuman: Decide whether the shared-balance solvency claim needs its own entry, or whether the constructor guard recommended in DEDUP-19-09 closes it.
